title: ST558 Project 1
text:
Our goal for this project is to write functions that will manipulate and process data sets from a census API. We’ll create generic functions to automatically summarize and plot certain returned data.


We are going to query the Public Use Microdata Sample (PUMS) Census API. Information about this is available here: Information about PUMS API

title: ST558 Project 1
text:
Parsing Variable Values
First, we’ll start by downloading and parsing the JSON files with variable descriptions for the years 2021-2024.

library(httr)
library(jsonlite)
library(tibble)

We only want to parse certain variables, so we’ll specify them below.
We want to write a function to GET() the URL, parse the JSON, and pull out a list of variables with their values. We’ll obtain one list for each year

vars <- c("AGEP", "GASP", "GRPIP", "JWAP", "JWDP", "JWMNP", "PWGTP",
               "FER", "HHL", "SCH", "SCHL", "SEX", "REGION", "DIVISION")
# ST: 2021-2022
# STATE: 2023-2024

#API Key - Required, should find some way to encrypt this in future
key <- "4270e8325c6e236168e18ec3682a2a6cc27469c7"

# Function
get_var_dict <- function(year) {
  if (!(year  %in% 2021:2024)) {
    stop("Year must be between 2021-2024")
  }
  
  url <- paste0("https://api.census.gov/data/", year, "/acs/acs1/pums/variables.json?key=", key)
  response <- GET(url)
  stop_for_status(response)
  parsed <- fromJSON(content(response, as = "text", encoding = "UTF-8"),
                             simplifyVector = FALSE)
  
  state_var <- if (year <= 2022) "ST" else "STATE"
  
  #For each variable, keep a named character vector and sort by numeric order
  lapply(parsed$variables[c(vars, state_var)], function(vector) {
    items <- unlist(vector$values$item)
    code_num <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(names(items)))
    items[order(is.na(code_num), code_num)]
  })
}

var_dicts <- lapply(2021:2024, get_var_dict)
names(var_dicts) <- 2021:2024

We can then save these lists as an .rds file in the repo under a data folder. Using dir.create() creates the folder from scratch, and rerunning it without warnings does nothing, allowing for more replicability.

dir.create("data", showWarnings = FALSE)
saveRDS(var_dicts, "data/var_dicts.rds")

Parsing API Data

# Testing via a hard-coded query
response <- GET(
  "https://api.census.gov/data/2024/acs/acs1/pums",
  query = list(
    get   = "SEX,PWGTP,AGEP",
    `for` = "state:37",
    key   = key
  )
)

parsed <- fromJSON(content(response, as = "text", encoding = "UTF-8"))
